38.h: 34 - Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib ʿAbd Manāf al-Hāshimī *
38.t:
The master, the martyr, of great standing, the banner of those who strive in jihad, Abū ʿAbd Allāh, the son of the paternal uncle of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, ʿAbd Manāf ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn (1) Quṣayy al-Hāshimī; the brother of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, and he was ten years older than ʿAlī.
He made both emigrations, and he emigrated from Abyssinia to Medina, reaching the Muslims while they were at Khaybar just after its capture. He stayed in Medina for some months; then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed him commander of the army of the expedition of Muʾtah, in the region of al-Karak, and he was martyred.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was greatly delighted at his arrival, and he grieved, by Allah, at his death.
He narrated a small amount.
Narrating from him: ابن مسعود، وعمرو بن العاص، وأم سلمة، وابنه عبد الله.
حديج بن معاوية: عن أبي إسحاق، عن عبد الله بن عتبة، عن ابن مسعود، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us to the Negus, eighty men: myself, Jaʿfar, Abū Mūsā, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUrfuṭah and ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn.
Quraysh sent ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ and ʿUmārah ibn al-Walīd with a gift. They came to the Negus, and when they entered they prostrated ⟦1:206⟧ to him and hastened to his side; one sat on his right and the other on his left, and they said:
A group of our people have settled in your land and have turned away from our religion.
He said: And where are they?
They said: In your land.
So he sent for them.
Jaʿfar said: I will be your spokesman.
So they followed him; he entered and gave the greeting of peace.
They said: Why do you not prostrate to the king?
He said: We prostrate to none but Allah.
They said: And why is that?
He said: Allah has sent among us a Messenger, and he commanded us to prostrate to none but Allah, and he commanded us to pray and to give zakat.
ʿAmr said: They oppose you (1) concerning the son of Maryam and his mother.
He said: What do you say about the son of Maryam and his mother?
Jaʿfar said: We say as Allah said: the spirit of Allah and His word, which He cast to the chaste virgin whom no man had touched.
He said: The Negus picked up a twig from the ground and said:
O assembly of Abyssinians, priests and monks! What do you want? This does not displease me! I bear witness that he is the Messenger of Allah, and that he is the one whom ʿĪsā foretold in the Gospel. By Allah, were it not for the kingship I am in, I would come to him and be the one who carries his sandals and brings him water for ablution.
And he said: Settle wherever you wish.
And he ordered that the other two's gift be returned to them, and it was returned.
He said: Ibn Masʿūd hastened back, and he took part in Badr (2) .
Something similar was narrated by: مجالد، عن الشعبي، عن عبد الله بن جعفر، عن أبيه (3) .
Something similar was narrated by: ابن عون، عن عمير بن إسحاق، عن عمرو بن العاص.
محمد بن إسحاق: عن الزهري، عن أبي بكر بن عبد الرحمن، عن أم ⟦1:207⟧ سلمة، قالت:
When Mecca became constricted for us, and the Companions (الصحابي) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were harmed and persecuted, and they saw the affliction that befell them, and that the Messenger of Allah could not ward it off from them, while he himself was protected by his people and his uncle, so that nothing he disliked of what befell his Companions (الصحابي) reached him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: (In the land of Abyssinia there is a king under whom no one is wronged; so go to his country until Allah grants you relief and a way out) .
So we went out to him in groups until we had gathered, and we settled in the best abode, with the best neighbour, secure in our religion (1) .
Al-Shaʿbī said: ʿAlī married Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays, and her two sons, Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr, boasted against each other.
Each of them said: My father is better than your father.
ʿAlī said: O Asmāʾ! Judge between them.
She said: I have not seen a young man better than Jaʿfar, nor a mature man better than Abū Bakr.
ʿAlī said: You have left nothing for us; had you said other than this, I would have detested you.
She said: By Allah, three of whom you are the least are indeed the best.
مجالد: عن الشعبي، عن عبد الله بن جعفر، قال:
I never asked ʿAlī for anything by the right of Jaʿfar but that he gave it to me.
ابن مهدي: حدثنا الأسود بن شيبان، عن خالد بن شمير، قال:
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rabāḥ came to us, and people gathered around him, and he said:
Abū Qatādah narrated to us, saying:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ dispatched the Army of the Commanders and said: (Zayd is over you; if he is struck down, then Jaʿfar; and if Jaʿfar is struck down, then Ibn Rawāḥah) .
Jaʿfar leapt up and said: May my father and mother be your ransom! I never feared that ⟦1:208⟧ you would appoint Zayd over me.
He said: (Go forth, for you do not know which of that is better) .
So the army set off, and they remained as long as Allah willed.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ascended the pulpit and ordered that it be called out: The prayer is gathering.
He ﷺ said: (Shall I not tell you about your army? They met the enemy, and Zayd was struck down a martyr, so seek forgiveness for him. Then Jaʿfar took the banner and charged at the people until he was killed. Then Ibn Rawāḥah took it and stood his ground until he was struck down a martyr. Then Khālid took the banner) .
He was not one of the appointed commanders; he appointed himself.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his two fingers and said: (O Allah (1) , he is one of Your swords, so grant him victory) .
From that day he was called: the Sword of Allah.
Then he said: (Go out and reinforce your brothers, and let no one stay behind) .
So the people went out in intense heat (2) .
ابن إسحاق: حدثنا يحيى بن عباد، عن أبيه، قال:
My foster father, who nursed me, and who was from Banū Murrah ibn ʿAwf, narrated to me, saying:
It is as if I am looking at Jaʿfar on the day of Muʾtah, when he leapt down from a sorrel mare of his and hamstrung her, then fought (3) until he was killed (4) .
Ibn Isḥāq said: He was the first in Islam to hamstring his mount, and he said: ⟦1:209⟧
How excellent is Paradise and its drawing near ... pure, and cool its drink
And the Byzantines are Byzantines whose punishment has drawn near ... it is upon me, if I meet them, to strike them
الواقدي: حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد بن عمر بن علي، عن أبيه، قال:
A Byzantine struck him and cut him in two halves, and in one of his halves were found thirty-odd wounds.
أبو أويس (1) : عن عبد الله، عن نافع، عن ابن عمر، قال:
We searched for Jaʿfar on the day of Muʾtah, and we found on him, between spear thrusts and arrow wounds, ninety-odd, and we found that on the front of his body (2) .
أسامة بن زيد الليثي: عن نافع، أن ابن عمر، قال:
I gathered Jaʿfar to my chest on the day of Muʾtah, and I found on the front of his body forty-odd wounds, between sword blows and spear thrusts (3) . ⟦1:210⟧
أبو أحمد الزبيري: عن عمرو بن ثابت، عن أبيه:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked about Jaʿfar, and a man said:
I saw him when a man pierced him with a spear; he walked toward him along the spear and struck him, and they both died together (1) .
سعدان بن الوليد: عن عطاء، عن ابن عباس:
While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting, with Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays nearby, he said: (O Asmāʾ! This is Jaʿfar, passing by with Jibrīl and Mīkāʾīl. He told me that he met the polytheists on such-and-such a day and gave the greeting of peace, so return his greeting) .
And he said: (He met the polytheists, and he was struck on his front seventy-three times. He took the banner in his right hand and it was cut off, then he took it in his left and it was cut off.
He said: So Allah gave me in place of my two hands two wings with which I fly with Jibrīl and Mīkāʾīl in Paradise, eating of its fruits (2)) .
And from Asmāʾ, who said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me and called for the sons of Jaʿfar; I saw him smell them, and his eyes shed tears.
I said: O Messenger of Allah! Has something reached you about Jaʿfar?
He said: (Yes, he was killed today) .
We stood up weeping, and he went back and said: (Prepare food for the family of Jaʿfar, for they have been kept from attending to themselves) (3) . ⟦1:211⟧
And from ʿĀʾishah, who said:
When the news of Jaʿfar's death came, we recognised grief in the face of the Prophet ﷺ (1) .
أبو شيبة العبسي: حدثنا الحكم، عن مقسم، عن ابن عباس:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (I saw Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib as an angel in Paradise, his wing feathers stained with blood, flying in Paradise (2)) .
عبد الله بن جعفر المديني: عن العلاء، عن أبيه:
From Abū Hurayrah, raised (المرفوع): (I saw Jaʿfar with two wings in Paradise) (3) .
Something similar has come from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Barāʾ, from the Prophet ﷺ.
It is said: He lived thirty-some years (may Allah be pleased with him). ⟦1:212⟧
عبد الله بن نمير: عن الأجلح، عن الشعبي، قال:
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from Khaybar, Jaʿfar met him; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ embraced him, kissed him between the eyes, and said: (I do not know which of the two makes me happier: the arrival of Jaʿfar or the conquest of Khaybar (1)) .
In the narration of Muḥammad ibn Rabīʿah, from Ajlaḥ:
He kissed him between his eyes, held him close, and embraced him.
Ibn Isḥāq said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ established brotherhood between Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib and Muʿādh ibn Jabal.
Al-Wāqidī rejected this and said: The brotherhood pact was only before Badr; then the verse of inheritance was revealed and the brotherhood pact ceased, and Jaʿfar was at that time in Abyssinia.
حفص بن غياث: عن جعفر بن محمد، عن أبيه:
That the daughter of Ḥamzah was wandering among the men when ʿAlī took her by the hand and handed her to Fāṭimah in her howdah. Then he, Jaʿfar and Zayd disputed over her.
ʿAlī said: She is my uncle's daughter, and I brought her out.
Jaʿfar said: She is my uncle's daughter, and her maternal aunt is my wife.
So he judged her in favour of Jaʿfar and said: (The maternal aunt is a mother) .
Jaʿfar stood and hopped around the Prophet ﷺ, circling him.
He said: (What is this?) .
He said: Something I saw the Abyssinians do for their kings (3) . ⟦1:213⟧
Her mother was Salmā bint ʿUmays, and her maternal aunt was Asmāʾ.
ابن إسحاق: عن ابن قسيط (1) ، عن محمد بن أسامة بن زيد، عن أبيه:
He heard the Prophet say to Jaʿfar: (Your physical form resembles my physical form, and your character resembles my character; you are of me and of my family tree (2)) .
إسرائيل: عن أبي إسحاق، عن البراء، وعن هبيرة بن مريم، وهانئ بن هانئ، عن علي، قالا (3) :
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Jaʿfar: (You resemble me in physical form and in character) (4) . ⟦1:214⟧
حماد بن سلمة، عن ثابت (ح) .
وعوف، عن محمد:
That the Prophet ﷺ said that to Jaʿfar (1) .
Al-Shaʿbī said: When Ibn ʿUmar greeted ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, he would say:
Peace be upon you, O son of the one with two wings (2) .
ابن إسحاق: عن الزهري، عن أبي بكر بن عبد الرحمن، عن أم سلمة - concerning their emigration to the land of the Negus, part of which has already passed - she said:
When Quraysh saw that, they agreed to send to him; so they sent ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Rabīʿah, and they gathered gifts for him and for his patriarchs.
They came to the king and said: Some foolish youths among us have abandoned our religion and have not entered your religion; they have brought a newly invented religion that we do not know, and they have taken refuge in your country, so we have been sent to you so that you return them.
His patriarchs said: They have spoken the truth, O king.
He became angry, then said: No, by the life of Allah, I will not return them to them until I speak with them; a people who have taken refuge in my country and chosen my protection. And nothing was more hateful to ʿAmr and Ibn Abī Rabīʿah than that the king should hear their speech.
When the messenger of the Negus came to them, the group gathered, and the one who spoke to him was Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib.
The Negus said: What is this religion?
They said: O king! We were a people upon polytheism: we worshipped idols, ate carrion, treated neighbours badly, and deemed lawful what is forbidden and the shedding of blood. Then Allah sent to us a Prophet from among ourselves, whose faithfulness, truthfulness and trustworthiness we knew, and he called us to worship Allah alone, to maintain ties of kinship, to treat neighbours well, to pray and to fast.
He said: Do you have anything of what he brought? - and he had summoned his bishops, ⟦1:215⟧ and he ordered them, and they spread out the scriptures around him -.
Jaʿfar said to them: Yes.
And he recited to them the opening of Sūrah {Kāf Hā Yā ʿAyn Ṣād} .
The Negus wept - by Allah - until his beard was wet, and his bishops wept until they wet their scriptures. Then he said:
This speech surely comes from the same lamp niche that Mūsā brought. Go, rightly guided; no, by Allah, I will not return them to you, nor will I gladden your eyes.
The two went out from him, and ʿAmr said:
I will come to him tomorrow with something by which I will uproot them, and he mentioned to him what they say about ʿĪsā (1) .
Shabāb said: ʿAlī, Jaʿfar and ʿAqīl: their mother was Fāṭimah bint Asad ibn Hāshim ibn ʿAbd Manāf.
Al-Wāqidī said: Jaʿfar emigrated to Abyssinia with his wife Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays, and there she gave birth to ʿAbd Allāh, ʿAwn and Muḥammad (2) .
Ibn Isḥāq said: Jaʿfar embraced Islam after thirty-one persons (3) .
إسماعيل بن أويس: حدثنا أبي، عن الحسن بن زيد:
That ʿAlī was the first male to embrace Islam, then Zayd embraced Islam, then Jaʿfar, and Abū Bakr was the fourth or the fifth.
Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir said: On the day of Badr the Messenger of Allah ﷺ allotted Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib his share and his reward.
It has been narrated through several routes:
That when Jaʿfar arrived, the Prophet ﷺ said: (I am more delighted by the arrival of Jaʿfar than by the conquest of Khaybar) (4) . ⟦1:216⟧
In one narration: he met him, embraced him and kissed him.
And in the (Ṣaḥīḥ), from the hadith of al-Barāʾ and others:
That the Prophet ﷺ said to Jaʿfar: (You resemble me in physical form and in character (1)) .
أحمد: حدثنا عفان، حدثنا وهيب، حدثنا خالد، عن عكرمة، عن أبي هريرة، قال:
No one who wore sandals or rode mounts after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was more excellent than Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib (2) .
Meaning: in generosity and nobility.
A group narrated it from Khālid, and it is muʿall (المعلل): it is narrated by عبيد الله بن عمرو، عن خالد، عن أبي قلابة، عن أبي هريرة.
ابن عجلان: عن المقبري، عن أبي هريرة، قال:
We used to call Jaʿfar the Father of the Poor. He would take us to his house, and if he found nothing for us, he would bring out to us a leather skin that had traces of honey; we would split it open and lick it (3) . ⟦1:217⟧
